messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — high p95 latency on inference API (us-west-2). Severity: page. PagerDuty: dispatched to #eng-oncall @here
Maya L.: ack, looking. seeing a spike in 95th and tail errors. grabbing dashboards now.
Maya L.: @Connor can you confirm if any deploys landed in us-west-2 in last 20m?
Connor: not from my side. I did a small cfg tweak ~2h ago in staging only.
Sanjay: I'm seeing a correlated increase in `kv-cache-miss-rate` and `request-queue-length` on the serving fleet.
Ava (sre): logs show repeated `ERROR: out_of_memory while allocating kv cache` from node g-04b. OOMs causing retries and timeouts.
Priya: customer reports: two customers in prod noticed slow responses and occasional 502s. Impact: degraded UX, not complete outage.
Maya L.: ok, mitigation plan: 1) remove g-04b from LB 2) switch model-route to smaller variant 3) lower batch size for live traffic. Doing step 1 now.
Connor: `kubectl cordon g-04b && kubectl drain g-04b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` (ran) — cordon/drain succeeded.
Maya L.: removing node improved tail latency by ~30ms so far. starting canary route to redwood-1b-quant instead of redwood-4b.
Sanjay: updating routing in runtime: `rdwctl route update --pool=us-west-2-prod --from=redwood-4b --to=redwood-1b-quant --pct=15`
incident-bot: ROUTE_CHANGE event logged (id: rchg-2026-02).
Priya: can we throttle background jobs? the async embed refreshers are spiking CPU and KV pressure.
Connor: toggled `embedding-refresher` to `pause=true` via feature flag. Confirming reduced background queue.
Ava (sre): tail metrics look stable but p99 still elevated. I recommend keeping smaller model until we validate KV cache behavior.
Maya L.: agreed. I'll monitor for 15m. handing off on-call to @Connor for the next 30m — need to take a quick call.
Connor: taking it. leaving notes: node g-04b drained, route partial to 1b-quant at 15%, batch size reduced to 8 from 16, embedding refresher paused.
(20m later)
Connor: p95 back to normal, p99 improving, no new OOMs. tagging incident-bot with status=mitigated.
incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED — no current pages. Start postmortem when stable.
Nadia (pm): thanks team. customers affected: two small enterprise tenants, support ticket numbers #54321, #54322. Can we get a customer impact blurb for comms?
Priya: brief: intermittent slow responses and some 502s for ~45m, mitigation by draining problematic node and temporary routing to smaller model; root cause looks like unexpected KV cache pressure leading to OOMs on a single host.
Maya L.: post-incident action items I propose: 1) add alert for `kv-cache-miss-rate` > 5% sustained 3m 2) make OOMs generate severity=sev2 ticket instead of page (unless >3 nodes) 3) dashboard tile for model route % per pool 4) playbook entry for quick model fallback command.
Connor: +1 on playbook and dashboard. Also suggest lowering paging sensitivity for `request-latency-p95` to trigger page only if `kv-cache-miss-rate` also high (reduce false positive pages).
Sanjay: can we tune the alert thresholds: current p95 page threshold = 350ms — maybe move to 500ms for pages and keep 350ms as ticket? Also add circuit-breaker metric: if node OOMs >= 2 in 10m then page.
Ava (sre): I can implement those in alerting this afternoon. Proposed diffs: - p95: page if >500ms for 3m AND kv-cache-miss-rate>5% - p95: ticket if >350ms for 5m without kv signal - OOMs: page if count>=2 in 10m, otherwise ticket.
Priya: for routing policy, let's make model-fallback route change a runbook step with a command snippet. Put runbook under docs/runbooks/model-fallback. Link in alert: `{{runbook:model-fallback}}`
Maya L.: I'll create the ticket and assign to eng-reliability for playbook/dashboard work. Ticket: RD-INC-937 (summary: kv-cache OOMs -> routing fallback + alert tuning).
Nadia (pm): for comms, I'll draft a short customer note and share with ops for review.
Connor: after action: we should also consider autoscaler safety limits — bump `min-eviction-memory` temporarily to avoid OOMs on node under KV pressure.
Maya L.: noted. thanks everyone. closing thread, followups in RD-INC-937 and a small PR for alerting. :thumbsup:
